name: Components and Interaction Rulebook
summary: Controls, overlays, feedback and behaviour that feel familiar and trustworthy.
check: Tab through every control and check every state.
Trigger every overlay: focus moves in, Escape closes, focus returns.

rules.title: Every control has all its states
rules.text: Default, hover, focus-visible, active/pressed, disabled, loading, error, and selected where it applies. A control without a focus style is unfinished.

rules.title: Standard controls stay standard
rules.text: Use native `<button>`, `<a>`, `<select>`, `<input>`, `<dialog>`, `<details>` or well-tested accessible components. Do not reinvent scrollbars, selects, checkboxes or date pickers for flavour; restyle them instead.

rules.title: Buttons look like buttons, links look like links
rules.text: Buttons for actions, links for navigation. Links in text are underlined or otherwise clearly distinct without relying only on colour.

rules.title: One button vocabulary
rules.text: Primary, secondary, tertiary (text) and destructive, the same shapes and sizes everywhere. If "Save" looks different on two screens, one is wrong.

rules.title: Target size
rules.text: Touch targets at least 44 × 44 px (24 × 24 px is the WCAG AA floor; aim for 44), with space between neighbours. Small icons get padding to reach it.

rules.title: Hover is a bonus
rules.text: Nothing important only appears on hover; touch screens have no hover. Hover effects never move the element away from the pointer or shift its neighbours.

rules.title: Modal is the last choice
rules.text: Prefer inline editing, expanding sections, a side sheet or a new page. Use a modal only for a focused task that must be finished or cancelled before going on.

rules.title: Dialogs done right
rules.text: `<dialog>` or an accessible equivalent: focus moves in, stays trapped, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger, background is inert, a visible close button and a clear title.

rules.title: Overlays escape their container
rules.text: Dropdowns and popovers use the popover API, `<dialog>`, `position: fixed` or a portal so `overflow: hidden` parents do not clip them.

rules.title: Toasts for confirmation, not for errors that need action
rules.text: Toasts disappear; anything the user must fix stays on the screen next to the cause (`ST-09`).

rules.title: Labels above fields, always visible
rules.text: Placeholders are examples, not labels.

rules.title: The right input
rules.text: `type="email"`, `tel`, `number` only for real numbers, `autocomplete` attributes, `inputmode`, and native pickers where they work well.

rules.title: Forgiving input
rules.text: Accept spaces in phone numbers and card numbers, trim whitespace, accept both decimal separators where the locale needs it.

rules.title: Preserve input
rules.text: Never clear a form after an error. Autosave long forms and drafts (`ST-08`).

rules.title: Undo over confirm
rules.text: For reversible actions (archive, remove from cart), act immediately and offer undo. Confirm only destructive, irreversible ones, and name what will be lost.

rules.title: Immediate feedback
rules.text: Every action responds within about 100 ms (pressed state, spinner on the button, optimistic update) and confirms its result (`DC-20`, `ST-10`).

rules.title: Keyboard and shortcuts
rules.text: Everything works with the keyboard in a logical order; frequent actions in apps get shortcuts (for example `/` for search, `⌘K` for a command menu) shown in tooltips or menus.

rules.title: Touch gestures have a fallback
rules.text: Swipe, drag and long-press always have a visible button alternative; drag surfaces set `touch-action` and clean up when a gesture is interrupted.

rules.title: Sticky actions on long forms and pages
rules.text: On long forms and product pages, the main action stays reachable (a sticky footer bar on phones) without covering content.

rules.title: Confirm destructive actions by name
rules.text: Irreversible actions say exactly what will be lost and use a specific button label ("Delete 3 invoices"), not "OK".

rules.title: Auto-rotating carousels
rules.text: No hero carousel that changes slides on its own. People miss the content and lose control; show the most important item, or let people move the carousel themselves with visible controls.

rules.title: Disabled buttons without a reason
rules.text: A disabled button says why (helper text or a tooltip), or stays enabled and explains what is missing when pressed.

rules.title: Essential information only in tooltips
rules.text: Tooltips are for hints. Anything needed to complete a task is visible on the page.

rules.title: Infinite scroll that hides the footer
rules.text: Infinite lists offer "Load more" or pagination when the footer, contact or legal links live below them.

rules.title: Custom cursors in working interfaces
rules.text: The system cursor stays in product UI and forms. Custom cursors are a style choice for portfolios and experiences only.

rules.title: Pop-ups on arrival
rules.text: No newsletter, discount or chat pop-up on page load or within the first scroll. Offer it inline or after a clear sign of interest.
